summary: The scope, the contracts and the session split can be executed as written, and most stack defaults hold: Spring MVC, MyBatis, Flyway and Maven are sound, and Java 17 as the language level matches Spring Boot 4's minimum. The parallel-run, cut-over and rollback steps are not safe as written. Four things must change before work starts. (1) The stack table says to reuse `.env` as is, but its defaults (`STONEHASH_DB_URL`, `BITCOIND_WALLET=attest`) point Java at the production schema and the live wallet. (2) Validation on a production replica must switch off outbound side effects (broadcasts, pending webhooks, partner calls) and compare against a second TypeScript instance, not `:8787`. (3) A rollback rule is missing. Flyway's free edition has no undo, so the rollback window must allow only additive migrations, and a rollback must mean restarting TypeScript on the same schema, not restoring a backup. (4) Times are ISO VARCHAR strings compared as text, so Java must write exactly the `toISOString()` shape. Next: the Flyway takeover needs a V1 baseline taken from the live schema and checked by a schema diff, a decision on the three boot-time data jobs, and migration as a separate step, because Spring Boot runs `migrate()` on startup by default. TypeScript changes made during the port need a matching contract test and migration. Stack facts checked on 2026-11-18: only Spring Boot 4.1 (OSS to 2027-07-31) and 4.0 (OSS ends 2026-12-31) are in open-source support, so 4.1.x should be pinned. Calling 21 the latest LTS is wrong; the latest is 25. BouncyCastle 1.85 and later has `BIP340Signer` but no BIP341, so the taproot code must still be ported. Remittance, the riskiest phase, should start alongside the others once the interfaces are fixed, and the double-entry ledger, which has no TypeScript counterpart, should come out of the port's completion criteria.

findings.problem: Every existing time column is a VARCHAR(40) holding `Date.toISOString()` output: always 3 fraction digits and a trailing Z. The code compares these columns and sorts them as text (session expiry, free-tier cleanup, webhook scheduling, keyset paging). Java's `Instant.toString()`, and Jackson's default output, write 0, 3, 6 or 9 fraction digits, and on Linux `Instant.now()` usually gives 6. Rows in mixed formats compare and sort wrongly ('Z' > '.' > digits), so paging can skip or repeat rows. TypeScript would also misread Java-written rows after a rollback. 'ISO 문자열' does not pin the format.

Section 4's job-queue claim needs skip-locked semantics. Oracle stores '' as NULL, and the code writes empty strings (user_agent). The document should name the branch points and how to split them (MyBatis `databaseId`, Flyway `{vendor}` folders), and pin the binary collation so keys and idempotency keys stay case-sensitive.

findings.where_in_doc: 2장 '암호' 행: 'Schnorr·탭루트는 BouncyCastle 또는 기존 구현 이식 중 택일'
findings.problem: This is not an either/or. BouncyCastle (1.85 and later; current API 1.87) ships `org.bouncycastle.crypto.signers.BIP340Signer` with x-only keys and 64-byte signatures, but it has no BIP341 support: no key tweak, script tree, sighash or control block. Those parts must be ported from btc/taproot.ts whichever way the choice goes. The TypeScript curve math is hand-written BigInt code that does not need porting. BC signs with random aux_rand by default and offers deterministic mode only with aux = 0^32, so reproducing signing vectors needs a fixed SecureRandom.
evidence: https://downloads.bouncycastle.org/java/docs/bcprov-jdk18on-javadoc/org/bouncycastle/crypto/signers/BIP340Signer.html ('Schnorr signatures for secp256k1 per BIP-340'; randomized by default; BIP340Signer(boolean deterministic) = aux_rand 0^32; no BIP-341 methods)

findings.proposed_text: | 암호 | JCA(P-256, SHA-256, HMAC, AES-GCM, ECDH)에 BouncyCastle(1.85 이상)을 더합니다: scrypt는 `SCrypt.generate`, BIP340 Schnorr는 `BIP340Signer`. 탭루트(BIP341: 키 트윅, 스크립트 트리, sighash, control block)는 BouncyCastle에 없으므로 `btc/taproot.ts`를 이식합니다. 곡선 연산은 `btc/secp256k1.ts`를 옮기지 않고 BouncyCastle 것을 씁니다 | 기존 `inscription`·`schnorr` 벡터와 BIP340 공식 벡터로 검증합니다. BouncyCastle은 기본이 무작위 서명이고 결정적 모드는 aux=0만 지원하므로, 서명 벡터는 aux_rand를 고정한 `SecureRandom`을 `ParametersWithRandom`으로 넣어 재현합니다 |

findings.problem: The contract leaves out details needed for byte compatibility: salt and hash are standard padded base64, the salt is 16 bytes, the key is 32 bytes, and verification reads N/r/p and the key length from the stored string, not from constants. Each hash needs about 128·N·r = 32 MiB, which is why Node raises maxmem. Node ran `scryptSync`, so hashes ran one at a time on the event loop. A Java servlet pool (about 200 threads) can run dozens at once and exhaust the heap during a login burst.
evidence: /home/ubuntu/bitcert-attest/attest/apps/core/src/account.ts:46 const SCRYPT = { N: 32_768, r: 8, p: 1, keylen: 32 }

findings.proposed_text: 비밀번호 해시 형식은 `scrypt$N$r$p$<솔트 base64>$<해시 base64>`입니다(표준 base64·패딩 포함, 솔트 16바이트, 키 길이 32바이트, 현재 N=32768·r=8·p=1). 검증 때는 N·r·p와 키 길이를 저장 문자열에서 읽고, 비밀번호는 UTF-8 바이트로 넣습니다. 해시 한 번에 약 32MiB를 씁니다. Node는 `scryptSync`라 한 번에 하나씩만 돌았으므로, Java에서는 동시 해시 수를 세마포어로 제한합니다(기본 2).
